commit_message:
[Bindings][Compiler] Add Bazel support for Python bindings

IREE's compiler Python support is available through CMake, but its generated
dialect bindings, native extensions and compiler tool wrappers are not exposed
as Bazel targets. Downstream projects using Bazel therefore need to maintain
their own build definitions to package Python bindings that match the compiler
they build.

Providing these targets upstream lets consumers build Python compiler packages
against their chosen IREE revision and keeps the binding definitions alongside
the sources they describe. The bindings use `IREECompiler`'s shared C API so
Python code can inspect and construct IR, then invoke the compiler using the
same MLIR implementation. Consumers retain control of package and wheel assembly.

commit_message:
[Compiler][Codegen] expose loop-return allocation control arg

Custom pipelines may return fresh buffers from loops and manage their
lifetime after bufferization. Empty-tensor analysis must honor the same
policy as bufferization so it does not reject otherwise supported IR,
while callers that do not opt in retain the existing equivalence requirement.

Co-authored-by: Luis Romero <115032777+L-roro@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Normalize contraction dimensions outside dispatches (#24965)

Contractions with several contiguous M, N, K or batch dimensions can
miss data-tiling encodings because dimension collapsing currently runs
inside dispatches.

Add a function pass that reuses the existing collapse rules outside
dispatches and restores the original tensor shapes at the op boundaries.
Leave existing dispatches (regions and workgroups) and ops with a preset
compilation info or lowering config alone, since those configurations
refer to the original loops.

No pipeline runs the pass yet. #24969 adds it to the experimental early
data-tiling route.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Normalize contraction dimensions outside dispatches (#24965)

Contractions with several contiguous M, N, K or batch dimensions can
miss data-tiling encodings because dimension collapsing currently runs
inside dispatches.

Add a function pass that reuses the existing collapse rules outside
dispatches and restores the original tensor shapes at the op boundaries.
Leave existing dispatches (regions and workgroups) and ops with a preset
compilation info or lowering config alone, since those configurations
refer to the original loops.

No pipeline runs the pass yet. #24969 adds it to the experimental early
data-tiling route.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

Assisted by AI.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Fuse packed contractions with epilogues and unpack

When contractions reach dispatch formation already packed, mmt4d ops
are not fused with their elementwise epilogues, and the result unpack
of mmt4d ops and data-tiled convolutions becomes a separate dispatch.

Add opt-in fusion of layout-preserving mmt4d epilogues and of the
result unpack. Epilogues must read the contraction result and write
their own result through identity maps. Only the unpack layouts that
data-tiling materialization produces are matched: row-major mmt4d
results, the transposed narrow-N form, and NHWC, NCHW and unit-batch
HWC convolution results. A group holds pack-like ops or the result
unpack, but not both.

The unpack is the last op of its group, so a consumer of a claimed
unpack gets its own dispatch instead of fusing with the unpack. An
unpack that its root does not claim becomes a root at its own position,
as without the options. Other fusion decisions are unchanged.

No pipeline enables the options yet. A follow-up enables them for
modules whose layouts are materialized before dispatch formation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: clang-tidy

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Add target-aware layout materialization

Dispatch-time data tiling assigns layouts inside dispatches, so the
phases before dispatch creation cannot see or propagate them.
Materializing the layouts during global optimization makes that phase
target aware on purpose: layouts propagate through the surrounding
tensor graph, and the packed contractions still fuse with their
epilogues and result unpacks.

Add the experimental --iree-opt-experimental-early-data-tiling flag. It
takes precedence over the other data-tiling placement flags, so
conflicting data-tiling flags are not an error when it is set, and the
route uses the operation families and encoding strategy of
dispatch-time data tiling.

The route applies to modules with a single llvm-cpu target on x86_64 or
AArch64 that uses the CPU encoding resolver without inner-tiled layouts,
and only with the default encoding strategy. For these modules, global
optimization propagates reshapes, normalizes contraction dimensions,
assigns and propagates encodings, and materializes them on the host. It
then records the target on the module, even if nothing was data-tiled.
Dispatch creation therefore skips encoding assignment for the whole
module, always fuses data-tiled ops with their epilogues and result
unpacks, and keeps the loop order of data-tiled convolutions. Other
modules keep dispatch-time data tiling. The enable_inner_tiled check
moves from the CPU encoding models to the Codegen utilities, so that the
eligibility check can share it.

On an Apple M3 Max (local-task, f32, median of 10), the route is within
noise of dispatch-time data tiling for a matmul with bias and ReLU, a
batch matmul with ReLU and a convolution with ReLU. x86_64 has not been
measured.

The layout decision is split over several passes, supports one CPU
target per module, and adds HAL and Codegen dependencies to the global
phases. The TODOs describe moving it into its own component that decides
per affinity.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: clang-tidy

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Propagate tensor encodings outside dispatch regions

Encoding propagation is currently tied to dispatch hoisting, which
prevents layout assignment from using the same rewrite rules on the
surrounding tensor graph.

Separate where propagation may happen from the rewrites themselves and
add a function pass for propagation outside dispatches. Keep the
existing hoisting behavior, and stop at existing dispatches and block
boundaries.

iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings runs in the dispatch-time
data-tiling pipeline and only swaps set_encoding ops with tensor.cast
producers, so adding these rewrites to it would change that pipeline.
Keep them separate until propagation through generic ops goes through
the encoding propagation interfaces.

Also stop bubbling set_encoding ops whose encoding is not an
EncodingAttr, such as a padding encoding, instead of crashing. Hoisting
already reached this within dispatches.

No pipeline runs the new pass yet. A follow-up adds it to an
experimental route that assigns and materializes data-tiling layouts
before dispatch formation.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Preserve the target of materialized tensor layouts

Once tensor layouts have been materialized for a device, dispatch
creation must neither assign encodings to them again nor compile them
for another device. Assigning encodings again re-encodes data-tiled
convolutions when convolutions are data-tiled, and tile shapes chosen
for one CPU can be unsupported or slow on another.

Record the target in a module attribute. Skip dispatch-time encoding
assignment for such modules, and reject them at the start of dispatch
creation when they are compiled for a different target, for several
targets, or for none. Modules without the attribute keep the existing
assignment, now wrapped in a module pass so that no function pass has
to read the attribute. Its options carry the operation families and
encoding strategy, so that printed pipelines and crash reproducers keep
them.

Nothing sets the attribute yet. A follow-up sets it in an experimental
route that materializes layouts during global optimization.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Add target-aware layout materialization

Dispatch-time data tiling assigns layouts inside dispatches, so the
phases before dispatch creation cannot see or propagate them.
Materializing the layouts during global optimization makes that phase
target aware on purpose: layouts propagate through the surrounding
tensor graph, and the packed contractions still fuse with their
epilogues and result unpacks.

Add the experimental --iree-opt-experimental-early-data-tiling flag. It
takes precedence over the other data-tiling placement flags, so
conflicting data-tiling flags are not an error when it is set, and the
route uses the operation families and encoding strategy of
dispatch-time data tiling.

The route applies to modules with a single llvm-cpu target on x86_64 or
AArch64 that uses the CPU encoding resolver without inner-tiled layouts,
and only with the default encoding strategy. For these modules, global
optimization propagates reshapes, normalizes contraction dimensions,
assigns and propagates encodings, and materializes them on the host. It
then records the target on the module, even if nothing was data-tiled.
Dispatch creation therefore skips encoding assignment for the whole
module, always fuses data-tiled ops with their epilogues and result
unpacks, and keeps the loop order of data-tiled convolutions. Other
modules keep dispatch-time data tiling. The enable_inner_tiled check
moves from the CPU encoding models to the Codegen utilities, so that the
eligibility check can share it.

On an Apple M3 Max (local-task, f32, median of 10), the route is within
noise of dispatch-time data tiling for a matmul with bias and ReLU, a
batch matmul with ReLU and a convolution with ReLU. x86_64 has not been
measured.

The layout decision is split over several passes, supports one CPU
target per module, and adds HAL and Codegen dependencies to the global
phases. The TODOs describe moving it into its own component that decides
per affinity.

name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Propagate tensor encodings outside dispatch regions

Encoding propagation is currently tied to dispatch hoisting, which
prevents layout assignment from using the same rewrite rules on the
surrounding tensor graph.

Separate where propagation may happen from the rewrites themselves and
add a function pass for propagation outside dispatches. Keep the
existing hoisting behavior, and stop at existing dispatches and block
boundaries.

iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings runs in the dispatch-time
data-tiling pipeline and only swaps set_encoding ops with tensor.cast
producers, so adding these rewrites to it would change that pipeline.
Keep them separate until propagation through generic ops goes through
the encoding propagation interfaces.

Also stop bubbling set_encoding ops whose encoding is not an
EncodingAttr, such as a padding encoding, instead of crashing. Hoisting
already reached this within dispatches.

No pipeline runs the new pass yet. A follow-up adds it to an
experimental route that assigns and materializes data-tiling layouts
before dispatch formation.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Propagate tensor encodings outside dispatch regions

Encoding propagation is currently tied to dispatch hoisting, which
prevents layout assignment from using the same rewrite rules on the
surrounding tensor graph.

Separate where propagation may happen from the rewrites themselves and
add a function pass for propagation outside dispatches. Keep the
existing hoisting behavior, and stop at existing dispatches and block
boundaries.

iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings runs in the dispatch-time
data-tiling pipeline and only swaps set_encoding ops with tensor.cast
producers, so adding these rewrites to it would change that pipeline.
Keep them separate until propagation through generic ops goes through
the encoding propagation interfaces.

Also stop bubbling set_encoding ops whose encoding is not an
EncodingAttr, such as a padding encoding, instead of crashing. Hoisting
already reached this within dispatches.

No pipeline runs the new pass yet. A follow-up adds it to an
experimental route that assigns and materializes data-tiling layouts
before dispatch formation.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Fuse packed contractions with epilogues and unpack

When contractions reach dispatch formation already packed, mmt4d ops
are not fused with their elementwise epilogues, and the result unpack
of mmt4d ops and data-tiled convolutions becomes a separate dispatch.

Add opt-in fusion of layout-preserving mmt4d epilogues and of the
result unpack. Epilogues must read the contraction result and write
their own result through identity maps. Only the unpack layouts that
data-tiling materialization produces are matched: row-major mmt4d
results, the transposed narrow-N form, and NHWC, NCHW and unit-batch
HWC convolution results. A group holds pack-like ops or the result
unpack, but not both.

The unpack is the last op of its group, so a consumer of a claimed
unpack gets its own dispatch instead of fusing with the unpack. An
unpack that its root does not claim becomes a root at its own position,
as without the options. Other fusion decisions are unchanged.

No pipeline enables the options yet. A follow-up enables them for
modules whose layouts are materialized before dispatch formation.

[DispatchCreation] Fuse packed contractions with epilogues and unpack

When contractions reach dispatch formation already packed, mmt4d ops
are not fused with their elementwise epilogues, and the result unpack
of mmt4d ops and data-tiled convolutions becomes a separate dispatch.

Add opt-in fusion of layout-preserving mmt4d epilogues and of the
result unpack. Epilogues must read the contraction result and write
their own result through identity maps. Only the unpack layouts that
data-tiling materialization produces are matched: row-major mmt4d
results, the transposed narrow-N form, and NHWC, NCHW and unit-batch
HWC convolution results. A group holds pack-like ops or the result
unpack, but not both.

The unpack is the last op of its group, so a consumer of a claimed
unpack gets its own dispatch instead of fusing with the unpack. An
unpack that its root does not claim becomes a root at its own position,
as without the options. Other fusion decisions are unchanged.

No pipeline enables the options yet. A follow-up enables them for
modules whose layouts are materialized before dispatch formation.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Add target-aware layout materialization

Dispatch-time data tiling assigns layouts inside dispatches, so the
phases before dispatch creation cannot see or propagate them.
Materializing the layouts during global optimization makes that phase
target aware on purpose: layouts propagate through the surrounding
tensor graph, and the packed contractions still fuse with their
epilogues and result unpacks.

Add the experimental --iree-opt-experimental-early-data-tiling flag. It
takes precedence over the other data-tiling placement flags, so
conflicting data-tiling flags are not an error when it is set, and the
route uses the operation families and encoding strategy of
dispatch-time data tiling.

The route applies to modules with a single llvm-cpu target on x86_64 or
AArch64 that uses the CPU encoding resolver without inner-tiled layouts,
and only with the default encoding strategy. For these modules, global
optimization propagates reshapes, normalizes contraction dimensions,
assigns and propagates encodings, and materializes them on the host. It
then records the target on the module, even if nothing was data-tiled.
Dispatch creation therefore skips encoding assignment for the whole
module, always fuses data-tiled ops with their epilogues and result
unpacks, and keeps the loop order of data-tiled convolutions. Other
modules keep dispatch-time data tiling. The enable_inner_tiled check
moves from the CPU encoding models to the Codegen utilities, so that the
eligibility check can share it.

On an Apple M3 Max (local-task, f32, median of 10), the route is within
noise of dispatch-time data tiling for a matmul with bias and ReLU, a
batch matmul with ReLU and a convolution with ReLU. x86_64 has not been
measured.

The layout decision is split over several passes, supports one CPU
target per module, and adds HAL and Codegen dependencies to the global
phases. The TODOs describe moving it into its own component that decides
per affinity.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Preserve the target of materialized tensor layouts

Once tensor layouts have been materialized for a device, dispatch
creation must neither assign encodings to them again nor compile them
for another device. Assigning encodings again re-encodes data-tiled
convolutions when convolutions are data-tiled, and tile shapes chosen
for one CPU can be unsupported or slow on another.

Record the target in a module attribute. Skip dispatch-time encoding
assignment for such modules, and reject them at the start of dispatch
creation when they are compiled for a different target, for several
targets, or for none. Modules without the attribute keep the existing
assignment, now wrapped in a module pass so that no function pass has
to read the attribute. Its options carry the operation families and
encoding strategy, so that printed pipelines and crash reproducers keep
them.

Nothing sets the attribute yet. A follow-up sets it in an experimental
route that materializes layouts during global optimization.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Propagate tensor encodings outside dispatch regions

Encoding propagation is currently tied to dispatch hoisting, which
prevents layout assignment from using the same rewrite rules on the
surrounding tensor graph.

Separate where propagation may happen from the rewrites themselves and
add a function pass for propagation outside dispatches. Keep the
existing hoisting behavior, and stop at existing dispatches and block
boundaries.

iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings runs in the dispatch-time
data-tiling pipeline and only swaps set_encoding ops with tensor.cast
producers, so adding these rewrites to it would change that pipeline.
Keep them separate until propagation through generic ops goes through
the encoding propagation interfaces.

Also stop bubbling set_encoding ops whose encoding is not an
EncodingAttr, such as a padding encoding, instead of crashing. Hoisting
already reached this within dispatches.

No pipeline runs the new pass yet. A follow-up adds it to an
experimental route that assigns and materializes data-tiling layouts
before dispatch formation.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Preserve the target of materialized tensor layouts

Once tensor layouts have been materialized for a device, dispatch
creation must neither assign encodings to them again nor compile them
for another device. Assigning encodings again re-encodes data-tiled
convolutions when convolutions are data-tiled, and tile shapes chosen
for one CPU can be unsupported or slow on another.

Record the target in a module attribute. Skip dispatch-time encoding
assignment for such modules, and reject them at the start of dispatch
creation when they are compiled for a different target, for several
targets, or for none. Modules without the attribute keep the existing
assignment, now wrapped in a module pass so that no function pass has
to read the attribute. Its options carry the operation families and
encoding strategy, so that printed pipelines and crash reproducers keep
them.

Nothing sets the attribute yet. A follow-up sets it in an experimental
route that materializes layouts during global optimization.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: clang-tidy

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Add target-aware layout materialization

Dispatch-time data tiling assigns layouts inside dispatches, so the
phases before dispatch creation cannot see or propagate them.
Materializing the layouts during global optimization makes that phase
target aware on purpose: layouts propagate through the surrounding
tensor graph, and the packed contractions still fuse with their
epilogues and result unpacks.

Add the experimental --iree-opt-experimental-early-data-tiling flag. It
takes precedence over the other data-tiling placement flags, so
conflicting data-tiling flags are not an error when it is set, and the
route uses the operation families and encoding strategy of
dispatch-time data tiling.

The route applies to modules with a single llvm-cpu target on x86_64 or
AArch64 that uses the CPU encoding resolver without inner-tiled layouts,
and only with the default encoding strategy. For these modules, global
optimization propagates reshapes, normalizes contraction dimensions,
assigns and propagates encodings, and materializes them on the host. It
then records the target on the module, even if nothing was data-tiled.
Dispatch creation therefore skips encoding assignment for the whole
module, always fuses data-tiled ops with their epilogues and result
unpacks, and keeps the loop order of data-tiled convolutions. Other

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Fuse packed contractions with epilogues and unpack

When contractions reach dispatch formation already packed, mmt4d ops
are not fused with their elementwise epilogues, and the result unpack
of mmt4d ops and data-tiled convolutions becomes a separate dispatch.

Add opt-in fusion of layout-preserving mmt4d epilogues and of the
result unpack. Epilogues must read the contraction result and write
their own result through identity maps. Only the unpack layouts that
data-tiling materialization produces are matched: row-major mmt4d
results, the transposed narrow-N form, and NHWC, NCHW and unit-batch
HWC convolution results. A group holds pack-like ops or the result
unpack, but not both.

The unpack is the last op of its group, so a consumer of a claimed
unpack gets its own dispatch instead of fusing with the unpack. An
unpack that its root does not claim becomes a root at its own position,
as without the options. Other fusion decisions are unchanged.

No pipeline enables the options yet. A follow-up enables them for
modules whose layouts are materialized before dispatch formation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: Analyze (python)

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Preserve the target of materialized tensor layouts

Once tensor layouts have been materialized for a device, dispatch
creation must neither assign encodings to them again nor compile them
for another device. Assigning encodings again re-encodes data-tiled
convolutions when convolutions are data-tiled, and tile shapes chosen
for one CPU can be unsupported or slow on another.

Record the target in a module attribute. Skip dispatch-time encoding
assignment for such modules, and reject them at the start of dispatch
creation when they are compiled for a different target, for several
targets, or for none. Modules without the attribute keep the existing
assignment, now wrapped in a module pass so that no function pass has
to read the attribute. Its options carry the operation families and
encoding strategy, so that printed pipelines and crash reproducers keep
them.

Nothing sets the attribute yet. A follow-up sets it in an experimental
route that materializes layouts during global optimization.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: Analyze (javascript)

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Propagate tensor encodings outside dispatch regions

Encoding propagation is currently tied to dispatch hoisting, which
prevents layout assignment from using the same rewrite rules on the
surrounding tensor graph.

Separate where propagation may happen from the rewrites themselves and
add a function pass for propagation outside dispatches. Keep the
existing hoisting behavior, and stop at existing dispatches and block
boundaries.

iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings runs in the dispatch-time
data-tiling pipeline and only swaps set_encoding ops with tensor.cast
producers, so adding these rewrites to it would change that pipeline.
Keep them separate until propagation through generic ops goes through
the encoding propagation interfaces.

Also stop bubbling set_encoding ops whose encoding is not an
EncodingAttr, such as a padding encoding, instead of crashing. Hoisting
already reached this within dispatches.

No pipeline runs the new pass yet. A follow-up adds it to an
experimental route that assigns and materializes data-tiling layouts
before dispatch formation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: Analyze (javascript)

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Normalize contraction dimensions outside dispatches (#24965)

Contractions with several contiguous M, N, K or batch dimensions can
miss data-tiling encodings because dimension collapsing currently runs
inside dispatches.

Add a function pass that reuses the existing collapse rules outside
dispatches and restores the original tensor shapes at the op boundaries.
Leave existing dispatches (regions and workgroups) and ops with a preset
compilation info or lowering config alone, since those configurations
refer to the original loops.

No pipeline runs the pass yet. #24969 adds it to the experimental early
data-tiling route.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

Assisted by AI.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Normalize contraction dimensions outside dispatches (#24965)

Contractions with several contiguous M, N, K or batch dimensions can
miss data-tiling encodings because dimension collapsing currently runs
inside dispatches.

Add a function pass that reuses the existing collapse rules outside
dispatches and restores the original tensor shapes at the op boundaries.
Leave existing dispatches (regions and workgroups) and ops with a preset
compilation info or lowering config alone, since those configurations
refer to the original loops.

No pipeline runs the pass yet. #24969 adds it to the experimental early
data-tiling route.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

[DispatchCreation] Normalize contraction dimensions outside dispatches (#24965)

Contractions with several contiguous M, N, K or batch dimensions can
miss data-tiling encodings because dimension collapsing currently runs
inside dispatches.

Add a function pass that reuses the existing collapse rules outside
dispatches and restores the original tensor shapes at the op boundaries.
Leave existing dispatches (regions and workgroups) and ops with a preset
compilation info or lowering config alone, since those configurations
refer to the original loops.

No pipeline runs the pass yet. #24969 adds it to the experimental early
data-tiling route.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

commit_message:
[Bazel] use execution paths for genrule inputs (#24981)

IREE's shared genrule definitions use rootpath for source files and
execpath for generated files so CMake can distinguish source and build
directories. In Bazel, however, rootpath describes runtime runfiles
paths, which break external IREE builds without legacy runfiles.
Translate these to execpath in the Bazel macro so build actions can
locate their inputs. Existing standalone IREE rules and CMake behavior
remain unchanged.

commit_message:
[CUDA] Preserve executable export names independently from PTX symbols (#24889)

## Motivation

While testing [Qwen3.8-27B](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B)
end-to-end with IREE, I found a CUDA executable lookup failure.

## Summary

CUDA executable serialization sanitizes kernel names for PTX, but
previously used that same sanitized name as the IREE executable export
identity.

This breaks modules whose generated dispatch names contain characters
that are not valid PTX symbols, such as `$`. Turbine-exported modules
can contain names such as `forward$async_dispatch_*`: compilation
succeeds, but CUDA executable creation fails at runtime.

This change stores the original IREE export name separately from the
sanitized PTX kernel symbol:

- `kernel_name` remains the sanitized symbol used by
`cuModuleGetFunction`.
- `export_name` preserves the original name used by
`hal.executable.lookup.function`.

`export_name` is an appended optional FlatBuffer field. Updated runtimes
fall back to `kernel_name` when loading older VMFBs that do not contain
it.


## Minimal reproduction

A standalone IREE module with a public function containing `$`
reproduces the failure:

```mlir
func.func @qwen$prefill(%input: tensor<4xf32>) -> tensor<4xf32> {
  %output = tensor.empty() : tensor<4xf32>
  %result = linalg.generic {
      indexing_maps = [
        affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>,
        affine_map<(d0) -> (d0)>
      ],
      iterator_types = ["parallel"]
    }
    ins(%input : tensor<4xf32>) outs(%output : tensor<4xf32>) {
      ^bb0(%in: f32, %out: f32):
        %scaled = arith.mulf %in, %in : f32
        linalg.yield %scaled : f32
    } -> tensor<4xf32>
  return %result : tensor<4xf32>
}
```

```
iree-compile repro.mlir \
  --iree-hal-target-backends=cuda \
  --iree-cuda-target=sm_120 \
  --iree-cuda-target-features=+ptx87 \
  -o repro.vmfb

iree-run-module \
  --module=repro.vmfb \
  --device=cuda \
  --function='qwen$prefill' \
  --input=4xf32=1
```

## Error
```
NOT_FOUND; function 'qwen$prefill' not found in executable
```
Changing only the public symbol to `@qwen_prefill` succeeds and produces
the expected result.

## Testing

Built `iree-compile` and `iree-run-module`, then ran the repro on CUDA
SM120 with PTX 8.7.
After this change it succeeds:

```text
EXEC @qwen$prefill
result[0]: hal.buffer_view
4xf32=1 1 1 1
```

commit_message: [PluginAPI] Support in-tree dynamic compiler plugins (#24894) Add CMake and Bazel build rules and in-tree examples for experimental dynamic compiler plugins. Preserve shared and system dependencies while resolving compiler symbols from the host, and test static and dynamic registration, duplicate registration, and helper dependencies. Make Bazel compiler tools link against the shared compiler library by default so dynamic plugins can resolve the required symbols. Opting into static compiler linking does not provide the exported ABI dynamic plugins need. Co-authored-by: Claude Code --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬 --------- Signed-off-by: Jelle Schühmacher Co-authored-by: Claude Code

`3.12.0.dev` to `3.13.0.dev`, so nightly releases are versioned
`3.13.0rcYYYYMMDD`.

The 3.12.0 release is promoted from `iree-3.12.0rc20260917`, so this
change does not affect it.

commit_message:
Version bump to 3.13 after 3.12 release (#24994)

Bumps `compiler/version.json` and `runtime/version.json` from
`3.12.0.dev` to `3.13.0.dev`, so nightly releases are versioned
`3.13.0rcYYYYMMDD`.

The 3.12.0 release is promoted from `iree-3.12.0rc20260917`, so this
change does not affect it.

Part of the release tracker #24993.

commit_message:
[iree-benchmark-module] Unify sync, async and dispatch execution (#24986)

`iree-benchmark-module` had separate synchronous, asynchronous, and
generated-dispatch execution paths that applied output processing,
replay capture, and profiling flushes inconsistently. Run them through
one batch lifecycle so discovery resolves each function's ABI and
iteration accounting once and every execution model shares the measured
loop.

The shared lifecycle fixes several inconsistencies:

- Retain asynchronous outputs for `--enable_output_processing`.
- Supply fence arguments for discovered asynchronous functions.
- Use the generated repeat count for dispatch benchmarks selected with
`--function`.
- Handle non-power-of-two `--batch_concurrency` without reading past the
invocation list.
- Return recording devices from context setup so asynchronous fences
participate in replay capture.

Errors go to stderr with `EXIT_FAILURE`, matching `iree-run-module`.
Output processing requires a single benchmarked function, and
nonpositive batch size or concurrency is rejected. Device profiling ends
before output processing.

Assisted by AI.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[iree-benchmark-module] Add dispatch timing rows

Add --dispatch_statistics for a per-function breakdown of where a
benchmark spends its dispatch time. After each measured repetition,
Google Benchmark reruns the registered benchmark outside the measured
interval with a lightweight HAL statistics session on every device, so
profiling uses the same function ABI, batch accounting and asynchronous
concurrency as measurement. The rows appear under their benchmark in
console, JSON and CSV output, including --benchmark_out files, whose
formatter is selected from Google Benchmark's parsed flags. Conflicting
profiling, capture and replay flags are rejected before any session
starts or the replay file is opened.

To start sessions with explicit options, the tooling profiling session
type is now iree_hal_profiling_session_t with _begin, _flush and _end
functions, and iree_hal_profiling_from_flags_is_requested validates the
profiling flags without starting a session. The device profiling flags
of iree-benchmark-module now cover every device instead of the first.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

benchmark spends its dispatch time. After each measured repetition,
Google Benchmark reruns the registered benchmark outside the measured
interval with a lightweight HAL statistics session on every device, so
profiling uses the same function ABI, batch accounting and asynchronous
concurrency as measurement. The rows appear under their benchmark in
console, JSON and CSV output, including --benchmark_out files, whose

profiling, capture and replay flags are rejected before any session
starts or the replay file is opened.

of iree-benchmark-module now cover every device instead of the first.

commit_message:
[iree-benchmark-module] Unify sync, async and dispatch execution (#24986)

`iree-benchmark-module` had separate synchronous, asynchronous, and
generated-dispatch execution paths that applied output processing,
replay capture, and profiling flushes inconsistently. Run them through
one batch lifecycle so discovery resolves each function's ABI and
iteration accounting once and every execution model shares the measured
loop.

The shared lifecycle fixes several inconsistencies:

- Retain asynchronous outputs for `--enable_output_processing`.
- Supply fence arguments for discovered asynchronous functions.
- Use the generated repeat count for dispatch benchmarks selected with
`--function`.
- Handle non-power-of-two `--batch_concurrency` without reading past the
invocation list.
- Return recording devices from context setup so asynchronous fences
participate in replay capture.

Errors go to stderr with `EXIT_FAILURE`, matching `iree-run-module`.
Output processing requires a single benchmarked function, and
nonpositive batch size or concurrency is rejected. Device profiling ends
before output processing.

Assisted by AI.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

[Torch] Name PT2E scale truncation and place map comments at their use

Rename createScaleOperand to truncateScalarScale, which is what it does
to per-tensor scales. Give getIndexingMaps a comment describing the maps
it returns and move the per-tensor/per-channel note to the parameter
map it explains. State what the torch-to-iree PT2E test checks: the
pipeline converts quantization to LinalgExt before Torch-to-Linalg.

commit_message:
[Bazel] use execution paths for genrule inputs (#24981)

IREE's shared genrule definitions use rootpath for source files and
execpath for generated files so CMake can distinguish source and build
directories. In Bazel, however, rootpath describes runtime runfiles
paths, which break external IREE builds without legacy runfiles.
Translate these to execpath in the Bazel macro so build actions can
locate their inputs. Existing standalone IREE rules and CMake behavior
remain unchanged.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Normalize contraction dimensions outside dispatches (#24965)

Contractions with several contiguous M, N, K or batch dimensions can
miss data-tiling encodings because dimension collapsing currently runs
inside dispatches.

Add a function pass that reuses the existing collapse rules outside
dispatches and restores the original tensor shapes at the op boundaries.
Leave existing dispatches (regions and workgroups) and ops with a preset
compilation info or lowering config alone, since those configurations
refer to the original loops.

No pipeline runs the pass yet. #24969 adds it to the experimental early
data-tiling route.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

Assisted by AI.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Propagate tensor encodings outside dispatch regions

Encoding propagation is currently tied to dispatch hoisting, which
prevents layout assignment from using the same rewrite rules on the
surrounding tensor graph.

Separate where propagation may happen from the rewrites themselves and
add a function pass for propagation outside dispatches. Keep the
existing hoisting behavior, and stop at existing dispatches and block
boundaries.

iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings runs in the dispatch-time
data-tiling pipeline and only swaps set_encoding ops with tensor.cast
producers, so adding these rewrites to it would change that pipeline.
Keep them separate until propagation through generic ops goes through
the encoding propagation interfaces.

Also stop bubbling set_encoding ops whose encoding is not an
EncodingAttr, such as a padding encoding, instead of crashing. Hoisting
already reached this within dispatches.

No pipeline runs the new pass yet. A follow-up adds it to an
experimental route that assigns and materializes data-tiling layouts
before dispatch formation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: Test Torch / test_torch_ops :: amdgpu_hip_gfx1201_O3

Encoding propagation is currently tied to dispatch hoisting, which
prevents layout assignment from using the same rewrite rules on the
surrounding tensor graph.

Separate where propagation may happen from the rewrites themselves and
add a function pass for propagation outside dispatches. Keep the
existing hoisting behavior, and stop at existing dispatches and block
boundaries.

iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings runs in the dispatch-time
data-tiling pipeline and only swaps set_encoding ops with tensor.cast
producers, so adding these rewrites to it would change that pipeline.
Keep them separate until propagation through generic ops goes through
the encoding propagation interfaces.

Also stop bubbling set_encoding ops whose encoding is not an
EncodingAttr, such as a padding encoding, instead of crashing. Hoisting
already reached this within dispatches.

No pipeline runs the new pass yet. A follow-up adds it to an
experimental route that assigns and materializes data-tiling layouts
before dispatch formation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[Compiler][Codegen] expose loop-return allocation control arg

Custom pipelines may return fresh buffers from loops and manage their
lifetime after bufferization. Empty-tensor analysis must honor the same
policy as bufferization so it does not reject otherwise supported IR,
while callers that do not opt in retain the existing equivalence requirement.

commit_message:
[Bindings][Compiler] Add Bazel support for Python bindings

IREE's compiler Python support is available through CMake, but its generated
dialect bindings, native extensions and compiler tool wrappers are not exposed
as Bazel targets. Downstream projects using Bazel therefore need to maintain
their own build definitions to package Python bindings that match the compiler
they build.

Providing these targets upstream lets consumers build Python compiler packages
against their chosen IREE revision and keeps the binding definitions alongside
the sources they describe. The bindings use `IREECompiler`'s shared C API so
Python code can inspect and construct IR, then invoke the compiler using the
same MLIR implementation. Consumers retain control of package and wheel assembly.

Assisted-By: GPT-6-Astra

commit_message:
[Bazel] use execution paths for genrule inputs (#24981)

IREE's shared genrule definitions use rootpath for source files and
execpath for generated files so CMake can distinguish source and build
directories. In Bazel, however, rootpath describes runtime runfiles
paths, which break external IREE builds without legacy runfiles.
Translate these to execpath in the Bazel macro so build actions can
locate their inputs. Existing standalone IREE rules and CMake behavior
remain unchanged.

Assisted By: GPT-6-Astra

[Bazel] use execution paths for genrule inputs (#24981)

IREE's shared genrule definitions use rootpath for source files and
execpath for generated files so CMake can distinguish source and build
directories. In Bazel, however, rootpath describes runtime runfiles
paths, which break external IREE builds without legacy runfiles.
Translate these to execpath in the Bazel macro so build actions can
locate their inputs. Existing standalone IREE rules and CMake behavior
remain unchanged.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Normalize contraction dimensions outside dispatches (#24965)

Contractions with several contiguous M, N, K or batch dimensions can
miss data-tiling encodings because dimension collapsing currently runs
inside dispatches.

Add a function pass that reuses the existing collapse rules outside
dispatches and restores the original tensor shapes at the op boundaries.
Leave existing dispatches (regions and workgroups) and ops with a preset
compilation info or lowering config alone, since those configurations
refer to the original loops.

No pipeline runs the pass yet. #24969 adds it to the experimental early
data-tiling route.

This is one of five PRs adding an experimental CPU path that
materializes data-tiling layouts before dispatch creation, so that
`linalg.mmt4d` and data-tiled convolutions fuse with their elementwise
epilogues and result unpacks.

Assisted by AI.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Propagate tensor encodings outside dispatch regions

Encoding propagation is currently tied to dispatch hoisting, which
prevents layout assignment from using the same rewrite rules on the
surrounding tensor graph.

Separate where propagation may happen from the rewrites themselves and
add a function pass for propagation outside dispatches. Keep the
existing hoisting behavior, and stop at existing dispatches and block
boundaries.

iree-dispatch-creation-propagate-encodings runs in the dispatch-time
data-tiling pipeline and only swaps set_encoding ops with tensor.cast
producers, so adding these rewrites to it would change that pipeline.
Keep them separate until propagation through generic ops goes through
the encoding propagation interfaces.

Also stop bubbling set_encoding ops whose encoding is not an
EncodingAttr, such as a padding encoding, instead of crashing. Hoisting
already reached this within dispatches.

No pipeline runs the new pass yet. A follow-up adds it to an
experimental route that assigns and materializes data-tiling layouts
before dispatch formation.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[Compiler][Codegen] expose loop-return allocation control arg

Custom pipelines may return fresh buffers from loops and manage their
lifetime after bufferization. Empty-tensor analysis must honor the same
policy as bufferization so it does not reject otherwise supported IR,
while callers that do not opt in retain the existing equivalence requirement.

commit_message:
[Bindings][Compiler] Add Bazel support for Python bindings

IREE's compiler Python support is available through CMake, but its generated
dialect bindings, native extensions and compiler tool wrappers are not exposed
as Bazel targets. Downstream projects using Bazel therefore need to maintain
their own build definitions to package Python bindings that match the compiler
they build.

Providing these targets upstream lets consumers build Python compiler packages
against their chosen IREE revision and keeps the binding definitions alongside
the sources they describe. The bindings use `IREECompiler`'s shared C API so
Python code can inspect and construct IR, then invoke the compiler using the
same MLIR implementation. Consumers retain control of package and wheel assembly.

Assisted-By: GPT-6-Astra

commit_message:
[iree-benchmark-module] Unify sync, async and dispatch execution (#24986)

`iree-benchmark-module` had separate synchronous, asynchronous, and
generated-dispatch execution paths that applied output processing,
replay capture, and profiling flushes inconsistently. Run them through
one batch lifecycle so discovery resolves each function's ABI and
iteration accounting once and every execution model shares the measured
loop.

The shared lifecycle fixes several inconsistencies:

- Retain asynchronous outputs for `--enable_output_processing`.
- Supply fence arguments for discovered asynchronous functions.
- Use the generated repeat count for dispatch benchmarks selected with
`--function`.
- Handle non-power-of-two `--batch_concurrency` without reading past the
invocation list.
- Return recording devices from context setup so asynchronous fences
participate in replay capture.

Errors go to stderr with `EXIT_FAILURE`, matching `iree-run-module`.
Output processing requires a single benchmarked function, and
nonpositive batch size or concurrency is rejected. Device profiling ends
before output processing.

Assisted by AI.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit_message:
[iree-benchmark-module] Add dispatch timing rows

Add --dispatch_statistics for a per-function breakdown of where a
benchmark spends its dispatch time. After each measured repetition,
Google Benchmark reruns the registered benchmark outside the measured
interval with a lightweight HAL statistics session on every device, so
profiling uses the same function ABI, batch accounting and asynchronous
concurrency as measurement. The rows appear under their benchmark in
console, JSON and CSV output, including --benchmark_out files, whose
formatter is selected from Google Benchmark's parsed flags. Conflicting
profiling, capture and replay flags are rejected before any session
starts or the replay file is opened.
